arabic_source:
٦٨٧٠ — عن أبي هريرة قال:
اقتتلت امرأتان من هذيل، فرمت إحداهما الأخرى بحجر فقتلتها وما في بطنها، فاختصموا إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
فقضى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن دية جنينها غرة: عبد أو وليدة، وقضى بدية المرأة على عاقلتها، وورثها ولدها ومن معهم.
فقال حمل بن النابغة الهذلي:
يا رسول الله ﷺ، كيف أغرم من لا شرب ولا أكل، ولا نطق ولا استهل؟ فمثل ذلك يطل.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
«إِنَّمَا هَذَا مِنْ إِخْوَانِ الْكُهَّانِ».
من أجل سجعه الذي سجع.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٩١٠)، ومسلم (١٦٨١/٣٦)، واللفظ لمسلم.
قوله: «على عاقلتها»: عاقلة الرجل قراباته من قبل الأب، وهم عصبته، وفيه أن الولد ليس من العاقلة، وأن العاقلة لا ترث إلا ما فضل عن أصحاب الفروض.
وقوله: «يطل»: أي يهدر ولا يضمن.
وفيه دليل على أن دية شبه العمد على العاقلة، بخلاف دية العمد فإنها على الجاني في ماله.

6870 — Abū Hurayrah reported:
Two women from Hudhayl fought, and one of them threw a stone at the other, killing her and the fetus in her womb. Their dispute was brought before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the compensation for the fetus was a ghurrah—a male or female slave. He ruled that the blood-money for the woman was to be paid by the killer’s ʿāqilah, and he assigned her inheritance to her children and the other heirs with them.
Ḥamal ibn al-Nābighah al-Hudhalī said:
“O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, how can I be made to pay compensation for one who neither drank nor ate, neither spoke nor cried at birth? Such a case should be disregarded.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“This man is only one of the brothers of the soothsayers,”
because of the rhyming manner in which he spoke.
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6910) and Muslim (1681/36). This is Muslim’s wording.
The expression “upon her ʿāqilah” refers to the paternal relatives who form the agnatic kin. This indicates that the child is not part of the ʿāqilah, and that the ʿāqilah inherits only what remains after the fixed-share heirs.
The word “yuṭall” means that it would be left without compensation.
It also shows that the blood-money for quasi-intentional killing is borne by the ʿāqilah, whereas the blood-money for intentional killing is borne by the offender from his own wealth.

«إِنَّمَا هَذَا مِنْ إِخْوَانِ الْكُهَّانِ».
من أجل سجعه الذي سجع.

“O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, how can I be made to pay compensation for one who neither drank nor ate, neither spoke nor cried at birth? Such a case should be disregarded.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“This man is only one of the brothers of the soothsayers,”
because of the rhyming manner in which he spoke.

٦٨٧١ — عن المغيرة بن شعبة، عن عمر رضي اللّٰه عنه:
أنه استشارهم في إملاص المرأة للمرأة.
فقال المغيرة:
قضى النبي ﷺ بالغرة: عبد أو أمة.
قال:
ائت بمن يشهد معك.
فشهد محمد بن مسلمة أنه شهد النبي ﷺ قضى به.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٩٠٥-٦٩٠٨)، ومسلم (١٦٨٩).

6871 — Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah reported that ʿUmar may Allah be pleased with him consulted the people concerning the case of one woman causing another woman to miscarry.
Al-Mughīrah said:
“The Prophet ﷺ ruled that the compensation was a ghurrah: a male or female slave.”
ʿUmar said:
“Bring someone who can testify along with you.”
Muḥammad ibn Maslamah then testified that he had witnessed the Prophet ﷺ give that ruling.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6905–6908) and Muslim (1689).

٦٨٧٢ — عن المغيرة بن شعبة قال: ضربت امرأة ضرّتها بعمود فُسطاط وهي حبلى، فقتلتها قال: وإحداهما لِحْيانية. قال: فجعل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ دية المقتولة على عصبة القاتلة. وغرةً لما في بطنها.
 فقال رجل من عصبة القاتلة: أنغرم دية من لا أكل ولا شرب ولا استهل؟ فمثل ذلك يطلّ! فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( أسجع كسجع الأعراب! )) قال: وجعل عليهم الدية.
 صحيح: رواه مسلم (٣٧:١٦٨٢).

6872 — Al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah said: A woman struck her co-wife with a tent pole while she was pregnant and killed her. One of the two women was from Lihyan. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the blood-money of the slain woman was upon the killer’s agnate relatives, and that there was a ghurrah for what was in her womb.
 A man from the killer’s agnate relatives said: “Are we to pay compensation for one who neither ate nor drank nor cried at birth? Such a thing should be disregarded.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Rhymed speech like the rhymed speech of the Bedouins?” Then he imposed the blood-money upon them.
 Authentic: narrated by Muslim (1682, no. 37).

 Authentic: narrated by Ibn Abi Asim in al-Diyat (171), al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar (4521), and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir (1/160).

6874 — Amr ibn Shuayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that a woman’s blood-money liability is borne by her agnate relatives, whoever they may be, and they inherit nothing from her except what remains after her heirs have received their shares. And if she is killed, then her blood-money goes among her heirs, and they are the ones entitled to retaliation against her killer.
 Sound: narrated by Ibn Majah (2647).

 حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٢٦٤٧).
6874 — Amr ibn Shuayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that a woman’s blood-money liability is borne by her agnate relatives, whoever they may be, and they inherit nothing from her except what remains after her heirs have received their shares. And if she is killed, then her blood-money goes among her heirs, and they are the ones entitled to retaliation against her killer.
 Sound: narrated by Ibn Majah (2647).

٦٨٧٥ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده قال:
كان رسول اللّٰه ﷺ يقوّم دية الخطأ على أهل القرى أربعمائة دينار، أو عدلها من الورق، ويقوّمها على أثمان الإبل؛ إذا غلت رفع في قيمتها، وإذا هاجت رخصاً نقص من قيمتها.
وبلغت على عهد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ما بين أربعمائة دينار إلى ثمانمائة دينار، وعدلها من الورق ثمانية آلاف درهم.
وقضى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ على أهل البقر مائتي بقرة، ومن كان دية عقله في الشاء فألفي شاة.
وقضى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن العقل ميراث بين ورثة القتيل على قرابتهم، فما فضل فللعصبة.
وقضى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ في الأنف إذا جدع الدية كاملة، وإن جدعت ثندوته فنصف العقل: خمسون من الإبل، أو عدلها من الذهب أو الورق، أو مائة بقرة، أو ألف شاة.
وفي اليد إذا قطعت نصف العقل.
وفي الرجل نصف العقل.
وفي المأمومة ثلث العقل: ثلاث وثلاثون من الإبل وثلث، أو قيمتها من الذهب أو الورق أو البقر أو الشاء.
والجائفة مثل ذلك.
وفي الأصابع في كل إصبع عشر من الإبل، وفي الأسنان في كل سن خمس من الإبل.
وقضى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ أن عقل المرأة بين عصبتها من كانوا، لا يرثون منها شيئًا إلا ما فضل عن ورثتها، وإن قتلت فعقلها بين ورثتها، وهم يقتلون قاتلهم.
وقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
«لَيْسَ لِلْقَاتِلِ شَيْءٌ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ وَارِثٌ فَوَارِثُهُ أَقْرَبُ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ، وَلَا يَرِثُ الْقَاتِلُ شَيْئًا».
قال محمد:
هذا كله حدثني به سليمان بن موسى، عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده، عن النبي ﷺ.
قال أبو داود:
محمد بن راشد من أهل دمشق، هرب إلى البصرة من القتل.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٥٦٤)، والبيهقي (٦/٢٢٠)، واللفظ لأبي داود.

6875 — ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb reported from his father, from his grandfather:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to assess the blood-money for accidental killing for the people of settled towns at four hundred dinars, or its equivalent in silver. He assessed it according to the market value of camels: when camels became expensive, he increased the amount, and when their prices fell, he reduced it.
During the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it ranged from four hundred dinars to eight hundred dinars, with its equivalent in silver being eight thousand dirhams.
He ruled that for people whose wealth consisted of cattle, the blood-money was two hundred cows, and for those whose wealth consisted of sheep, two thousand sheep.
He ruled that blood-money is inherited among the heirs of the slain person according to their degrees of kinship, and whatever remains goes to the agnatic relatives.
He ruled that if the nose is completely cut off, the full blood-money is due. If only the soft end of the nose is severed, half the blood-money is due: fifty camels, or their equivalent in gold or silver, or one hundred cows, or one thousand sheep.
For a severed hand, half the blood-money is due.
For one leg, half the blood-money is due.
For a head wound reaching the membrane surrounding the brain, one-third of the blood-money is due: thirty-three and one-third camels, or their equivalent in gold, silver, cattle, or sheep.
A penetrating wound into the body cavity carries the same amount.
For each finger, ten camels are due, and for each tooth, five camels.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also ruled that a woman’s blood-money liability is borne by her agnatic relatives, whoever they may be. They do not inherit from her except what remains after her heirs have received their shares. If she is killed, her blood-money belongs to her heirs, and they have the right of retaliation against her killer.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ also said:
“The killer receives nothing. If the deceased has no heir, then his heir is the closest person to him, and the killer inherits nothing.”
Muḥammad said:
“Sulaimān ibn Mūsā narrated all of this to me from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet ﷺ.”
Abū Dāwūd said:
“Muḥammad ibn Rāshid was from the people of Damascus and fled to Baṣrah because of a killing.”
Good: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4564) and al-Bayhaqī (6/220). This is the wording of Abū Dāwūd.

6876 — Amr ibn Shuayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that for the blind eye which remains in place, if it is destroyed, one-third of its blood-money is due. For a paralyzed hand, if it is cut off, one-third of its blood-money is due. And for a blackened tooth, if it is removed, one-third of its blood-money is due.
 Sound: narrated by al-Nasai (4840) and Abu Dawud (4567).

6876 — Amr ibn Shuayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that for the blind eye which remains in place, if it is destroyed, one-third of its blood-money is due. For a paralyzed hand, if it is cut off, one-third of its blood-money is due. And for a blackened tooth, if it is removed, one-third of its blood-money is due.
 Sound: narrated by al-Nasai (4840) and Abu Dawud (4567).

٦٨٧٧ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده أن النبي ﷺ قال: (( في المواضح خمس)).
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٥٦٦) والترمذي (١٣٩٠) وحسّنه، والنسائي (٤٨٥٢) وابن ماجه (٢٦٥٥).
 خمس من الإبل.
 والموضحة هي الشجة التي توضح العظم - أي تظهره. وهي في الغالب ما تكون في الوجه والرأس.

english_source:
6877 — Amr ibn Shuayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet ﷺ said: “For the wound that exposes the bone, there are five.”
 Sound: narrated by Abu Dawud (4566), al-Tirmidhi (1390), who graded it sound, al-Nasai (4852), and Ibn Majah (2655).
 That means five camels.
 A muwaddihah is a head or facial wound that exposes the bone, meaning it makes it visible. It is usually found on the face or head.

arabic_source: ٦٨٧٨ — عن ابن عباس، عن النبي ﷺ قال: (( هذه وهذه سواء ))، يعني الخنصر والإبهام. وفي رواية: (( الأصابع سواء، والأسنان سواء، الثنية والضرس سواء، هذه وهذه سواء )). صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٨٩٥). ورواه أبو داود (٤٥٥٩) وابن الجارود (٧٨٣).

english_source:
6878 — Ibn Abbas narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: “This and this are equal,” meaning the little finger and the thumb are equal. “The teeth are equal as well; the front tooth and the molar are equal. This and this are equal.”
 Authentic: narrated by al-Bukhari (6895). It was also narrated by Abu Dawud (4559) and Ibn al-Jarud (783), and in that wording it says: “The fingers are equal.”

٦٨٧٩ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عباس قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( دية الأصابع اليدين والرجلين
 سواء. عشرة من الإبل لكل أصبع )).
 صحيح: رواه الترمذي (١٣٩١) واللفظ له، وأبو داود (٤٥٦٠،٤٥٦١) والنسائي (٤٨٤٩) وابن
 الجارود (٧٨٠).

6879 — Abdullah ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The blood-money for the fingers of the hands and feet is equal: ten camels for each finger.”
 Authentic: narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1391), and this is his wording, as well as Abu Dawud (4560, 4561), al-Nasai (4849), and Ibn al-Jarud (780).

٦٨٨٣ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عمرو أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ خطب يوم فتح مكة، فكبّر ثلاثا ثم قال: (( لا إله إلا اللّٰه وحده، صدق وعده، ونصر عبده، وهزم الأحزاب وحده، ألا إن كل مأثرةٍ كانت في الجاهلية تذكر وتُدعى من دم، أو مال تحت قدميَّ، إلا ماكان من سقاية الحاج، وسدانة البيت)). ثم قال: (( ألا إن دية الخطأ شبه العمد ما كان بالسوط والعصا مائة من الإبل: منها أربعون في بطونها أولادها )).
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٥٤٧) وابن ماجه (٢٦٢٧) وابن الجارود (٧٧٣) وصحّحه ابن حبان
 (٦٠١١).

english_source:
6883 — Abdullah ibn Amr reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon on the day of the conquest of Makkah. He said the takbir three times, then said: “There is no god but Allah alone. He fulfilled His promise, gave victory to His servant, and defeated the confederates alone. Indeed, every claim of distinction from the pre-Islamic period, whether in blood or wealth, is beneath my feet, except the giving of water to the pilgrims and the custodianship of the House.” Then he said: “Indeed, the blood-money for quasi-intentional mistaken killing, when done with a whip or a stick, is one hundred camels, forty of which are pregnant.”
 Sound: narrated by Abu Dawud (4547), Ibn Majah (2627), and Ibn al-Jarud (773), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (6011).

٦٨٨٤ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قضى أن من قتل خطأ فديته مائة من الإبل: ثلاثون بنت مخاض، وثلاثون بنت لبون، وثلاثون حقة، وعشر بنو لبون ذكر.
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٤٥٤١) وابن ماجه ( ٢٦٣٠) والدار قطني (٩٥ /٣) واللفظ لأبي داود.

english_source:
6884 — Amr ibn Shuayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that whoever kills by mistake, his blood-money is one hundred camels: thirty bint makhad, thirty bint labun, thirty hiqqah, and ten male banu labun.
 Sound: narrated by Abu Dawud (4541), Ibn Majah (2630), and al-Daraqutni (3/95). This wording is from Abu Dawud.

arabic_source:
٦٨٨٥ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده قال: كانت قيمة الدية في عهد رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ثمانمائة دينار، أو ثمانية آلاف درهم، ودية أهل الكتاب يومئذ النصف من دية المسلمين. قال: فكان ذلك كذلك حتى استخلف عمر فقام خطيباً فقال: ألا إن الإبل قد غلتْ، ففرضها عمر على أهل الذهب ألف دينار، وعلى أهل الورق اثني عشر ألف درهم، وعلى أهل البقر مائتي بقرة، وعلى أهل الشاء ألفي شاة، وعلى أهل الحلل مائتي حلة، قال: وترك دية أهل الذمة لم يرفعها فيما رفع من الدية.
 حسن: رواه ابو داود ( ٤٥٤٢).

english_source:
6885 — Amr ibn Shuayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The value of the blood-money during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was eight hundred dinars or eight thousand dirhams, and the blood-money of the People of the Book at that time was half that of the Muslims. This remained so until Umar became caliph. Then he stood and addressed the people, saying: “Indeed, camels have become expensive.” So Umar fixed it for the people of gold at one thousand dinars, for the people of silver at twelve thousand dirhams, for the people of cattle at two hundred cows, for the people of sheep at two thousand sheep, and for the people of garments at two hundred garments. He left the blood-money of the protected non-Muslims unchanged and did not raise it as he raised the blood-money.
 Sound: narrated by Abu Dawud (4542).

arabic_source:
٦٨٨٦ — عن عمرو بن شعيب، عن أبيه، عن جده، قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ (( المسلمون تتكافأ دماؤهم: يسعى بذمتهم أدناهم، ويجير عليه أقصاهم، وهم يد على من سواهم، يرد مشدهم على مُضْعفهم، ومتسريهم على قاعدهم، لا يُقتل مؤمن بكافر، ولا ذو عهد في عهده ))
 وفي رواية: (( دية عقل الكافر نصف دية عقل المؤمن ))
 حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٧٥١) والترمذي (١٤١٣) وحسّنه، والنسائي (٤٨٠٦) والرواية الثانية عند الترمذي.

english_source:
6886 — Amr ibn Shuayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The blood of the Muslims is equal. The lowest among them may grant protection on behalf of them all, and the farthest among them may guarantee protection. They are united against others. Those with quick mounts should return to those with slow mounts, and those who go out with a detachment should return to those who remain stationed. A believer is not killed in retaliation for a disbeliever, nor one under covenant while he remains under his covenant.”
 In another narration: “The blood-money of a disbeliever is half the blood-money of a believer.”
 Sound: narrated by Abu Dawud (2751), al-Tirmidhi (1413), who graded it sound, and al-Nasai (4806). The second narration is in al-Tirmidhi.

٦٨٨٧ — عن عائشة، أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ بعث أبا جهم بن حذيفة مصدقا، فلاجَّه رجل في صدقته، فضربه أبو جهم، فشجَّه، فأتوا النبي ﷺ فقالوا: القودَ يا رسول الله ﷺ! فقال النبي ﷺ: (( لكم
 كذا وكذا)) فلم يرضوا، فقال: (( لكم كذا وكذا)) فرضوا، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( إني خاطب العشية على الناس ومخبرهم برضاكم؟ )) قالوا: نعم. فخطب النبي ﷺ قال: (( إن هؤلاء الليثيين أتوني يريدون القود، فعرضت عليهم كذا وكذا فرضوا، أرضيتم؟ )) قالوا: لا. فهم بهم المهاجرون، فأمر النبي ﷺ أن يكفوا عنهم، فكفوا، ثم دعاهم فزادهم، فقال: (( أرضيتم؟ )) قالوا: نعم، قال: (( إني خاطب على الناس ومخبرهم برضاكم)) قالوا: نعم، فخطب النبي ﷺ فقال: (( أرضيتم؟ )) قالوا: نعم.
 صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٥٣٤) والنسائي (٤٧٧٨) وابن ماجه (٢٦٣٨) وصحّحه ابن حبان (٤٤٨٧).

6887 — Aishah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah as a collector. A man disputed with him over his due, so Abu Jahm struck him and wounded his head. They came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “Retaliation, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” The Prophet ﷺ said: “You will have such-and-such,” but they were not satisfied. Then he said: “You will have such-and-such,” and they were satisfied. Then the Prophet ﷺ said: “I will address the people this evening and inform them of your acceptance. Is that agreeable to you?” They said: “Yes.” So the Prophet ﷺ addressed the people and said: “These people from Layth came to me wanting retaliation, and I offered them such-and-such and they accepted. Are you satisfied?” They said: “No.” The Emigrants moved toward them, but the Prophet ﷺ ordered them to leave them alone, so they stopped. Then he called them again and increased the offer to them, and said: “Are you satisfied?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “I will address the people and inform them of your acceptance.” They said: “Yes.” So he addressed the people and said: “Are you satisfied?” They said: “Yes.”
 Authentic: narrated by Abu Dawud (4534), al-Nasai (4778), Ibn Majah (2638), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (4487).

arabic_source: ٦٨٨٨ — عن أبي رِمثة قال: انطلقت مع أبي نحو النبي ﷺ، فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ لأبي: (( ابنك هذا؟ )) قال: إي ورب الكعبة. قال: (( حقاً؟ )) قال: أشهد به. فتبسم رسول اللّٰه ﷺ ضاحكاً من ثَبَت شبهي في أبي، ومن حلف أبي عليّ. ثم قال: (( أما إنه لا يجني عليك ولا تجني عليه )) وقرأ: ﴿وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ﴾ [فاطر: ١٨]. صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٤٩٥)، والنسائي (١٥٧٢)، والترمذي (٢٨١٢)، وأحمد (٧١٠٩). واللفظ لأبي داود.

6888 — Abu Rimthah said: I went with my father to the Prophet ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to my father: “Is this your son?” He said: “Yes, by the Lord of the Ka’bah.” He said: “Truly?” He said: “I bear witness to it.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled, laughing at my resemblance to my father and at my father’s oath concerning me. Then he said: “Indeed, he does not bear your crime, nor do you bear his crime.” Then he recited: “No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.” [Fatir: 18]
 Authentic: narrated by Abu Dawud (4495), al-Nasai (1572), al-Tirmidhi (2812), and Ahmad (7109). This wording is from Abu Dawud.

٦٨٩٠ — عن طارق المحاربي أن رجلاً قال: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ هؤلاء بنو ثعلبة الذين قتلوا فلانا في الجاهلية فخذ لنا بثأرنا. فرفع يديه حتى رأيت بياض إبطيه وهو يقول: (( لا تجني أم على ولد مرتين)).
 حسن: رواه النسائي (٤٨٣٩) وابن ماجه (٢٦٧٠) واللفظ لهما وصحّحه ابن حبان (٦٥٦٢).

6890 — Tariq al-Muharibi reported that a man said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, these are Banu Tha’labah who killed so-and-so in the pre-Islamic period, so take revenge for us.” The Prophet ﷺ raised his hands until I could see the whiteness of his armpits and said: “A mother is not held liable for her child twice.”
 Sound: narrated by al-Nasai (4839) and Ibn Majah (2670), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (6562).

 حسن: رواه النسائي (٤٨٣٩) وابن ماجه (٢٦٧٠) واللفظ لهما وصحّحه ابن حبان (٦٥٦٢).
6890 — Tariq al-Muharibi reported that a man said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, these are Banu Tha’labah who killed so-and-so in the pre-Islamic period, so take revenge for us.” The Prophet ﷺ raised his hands until I could see the whiteness of his armpits and said: “A mother is not held liable for her child twice.”
 Sound: narrated by al-Nasai (4839) and Ibn Majah (2670), and authenticated by Ibn Hibban (6562).

 حسن: رواه ابن ماجه (٢٦٧٢).

 فقالوا: يا رسول اللّٰه ﷺ هؤلاء بنو ثعلبة بن يربوع قتلوا فلانا في الجاهلية فقال النبي ﷺ وهتف بصوته:
 (( ألا لا تجني نفس على الأخرى ))
 صحيح: رواه النسائي (٤٨٣٣)، وأحمد (١٦٦١٣).

٦٨٩٣ — عن عمران بن الحصين:
أن غلامًا لأناس فقراء قطع أذن غلام لأناس أغنياء، فأتى أهله النبي ﷺ فقالوا:
يا رسول الله ﷺ، إنا أناس فقراء.
فلم يجعل عليه شيئًا.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٤٥٩٠)، والنسائي (٤٧٥١). 
والغلام معناه الولد الصغير، والظاهر من السياق أنه كان حرًّا، وجنايته كانت خطأ، وكانت عاقلته فقراء. وكذلك الغلام المجني عليه كان حرًّا؛ لأنه لو كان عبدًا لم يكن لاعتذار أهله بالفقر معنى، لأن العاقلة لا تحمل عبدًا، كما لا تحمل عمدًا ولا اعترافًا، في قول أكثر أهل العلم كما قال الخطابي.
وقد فهم النسائي وأبو داود أن المراد بالغلام العبد، فلو كان هذا صحيحًا فإن الغلام المملوك إذا جنى على عبد أو حر فجنايته في رقبته، في قول عامة الفقهاء.

english_source:
6893 — ʿImrān ibn al-Ḥuṣayn reported:
A young boy belonging to some poor people cut off the ear of a boy belonging to some wealthy people. His family came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
“O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we are poor people.”
So he imposed nothing upon him.
Authentic: Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4590) and al-Nasāʾī (4751). 
The word ghulām means a young boy. The apparent meaning of the context is that he was free and that his offense was accidental, while his ʿāqilah were poor. The injured boy likewise appears to have been free; had he been a slave, there would have been no point in the family pleading poverty, because the ʿāqilah does not bear liability for injury to a slave, nor for an intentional offense, nor for liability established by confession, according to most scholars, as al-Khaṭṭābī stated.
Al-Nasāʾī and Abū Dāwūd understood ghulām here as meaning a slave. If that understanding is correct, then when an enslaved boy injures a slave or a free person, the liability is attached to his person, according to the majority of jurists.

٦٨٩٤ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: (( جرح العجماء جبار، والبئر جبار، والمعدن جبار، وفي الركاز الخمس )).
 متفق عليه: رواه مالك (٤٢)، والبخاري (٦٩١٢)، ومسلم (١٧١٠).
 والعجماء: البهيمة، وسميت العجماء لأنها لا تتكلم. وقوله: جبار أي هدر، لا دية فيه.
 وقوله: البئر جبار: أي أن الإنسان لو حفر بئراً في مِلكه أو في موات فوقع فيها إنسان فلا ضمان عليه.

6894 — Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The injury caused by an animal is without liability, a well is without liability, a mine is without liability, and one-fifth is due on buried treasure.”
 Agreed upon: narrated by Malik (42), al-Bukhari (6912), and Muslim (1710).
 The word al-ajma’ means an animal, and it is called that because it does not speak. The phrase jubar means it is not subject to compensation, with no blood-money due for it.
 The phrase “a well is without liability” means that if a person digs a well on his own property or in unused land and someone falls into it, he is not liable.

٦٨٩٥ — عن عمران بن الحصين:
أن رجلًا عض يد رجل، فنزع يده من فمه فوقعت ثنيتاه، فاختصموا إلى النبي ﷺ فقال:
«يَعَضُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَخَاهُ كَمَا يَعَضُّ الْفَحْلُ؟ لَا دِيَةَ لَهُ».
وفي لفظ: فرفع إلى النبي ﷺ فأبطله، وقال:
«أَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَأْكُلَ لَحْمَهُ؟!»
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٨٩٢)، ومسلم (١٦٧٣/١٨). واللفظ الثاني رواه مسلم من وجه آخر.

6895 — ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn reported:
A man bit another man’s hand. The other man pulled his hand from the biter’s mouth, causing the biter’s two front teeth to fall out. They brought their dispute before the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
“Would one of you bite his brother as a stallion bites? He is entitled to no blood-money.”
In another wording, the matter was brought before the Prophet ﷺ, and he dismissed the claim and said:
“Did you intend to eat his flesh?!”

٦٨٩٦ — عن عمران بن الحصين:
أن رجلًا عض يد رجل، فانتزع يده، فسقطت ثنيته أو ثناياه، فاستعدى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
فقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ:
«مَا تَأْمُرُنِي؟ تَأْمُرُنِي أَنْ آمُرَهُ أَنْ يَدَعَ يَدَهُ فِي فِيكَ تَقْضَمُهَا كَمَا يَقْضَمُ الْفَحْلُ؟! ادْفَعْ يَدَكَ حَتَّى يَعَضَّهَا ثُمَّ انْتَزِعْهَا».
صحيح: رواه مسلم (١٦٧٣/٢١).
وأشار الحافظ إلى هذه الرواية في الفتح (١٢/٢٢١)، ثم قال: وعند أبي نعيم في المستخرج من الوجه الذي أخرجه مسلم:
«إِنْ شِئْتَ أَمَرْنَاهُ فَعَضَّ يَدَكَ ثُمَّ انْتَزَعْهَا أَنْتَ».
والأمر الوارد في رواية مسلم على التخيير وليس على الإلزام، ثم أهدر النبي ﷺ ثنيته.

6896 — ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn reported:
A man bit another man’s hand. The man pulled his hand away, causing one or more of the biter’s front teeth to fall out. The biter then sought judgment from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
“What do you want me to order? Do you want me to order him to leave his hand in your mouth so that you may bite it as a stallion bites? Put your hand forward until he bites it, then pull it away.”
Authentic: Narrated by Muslim (1673/21).
Al-Ḥāfiẓ referred to this narration in Fatḥ al-Bārī (12/221) and stated that Abū Nuʿaym’s al-Mustakhraj, through the same route as Muslim, has the wording:
“If you wish, we will order him to let you bite his hand, then you may pull it away yourself.”
The command in Muslim’s narration indicates an option, not an obligation. The Prophet ﷺ then ruled that no compensation was due for the biter’s tooth.

٦٨٩٨ — عن أنس بن مالك، أن رجلاً اطلع في بعض حُجر النبي ﷺ فقام إليه بمشقص - أو مشاقص - ، وجعل يختِله ليطعنه.
 متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٩٠٠) ومسلم (٢١٥٨).
 قوله: “مشاقص “ جمع مشقص وهو نصل عريض للسهم. وقوله: “ويختله” بفتح أوله وكسر التاء أي يراوغه ويستغفله.

arabic_source: ٦٨٩٩ — عن سهل بن سعد أخبره أن رجلاً اطّلع في جحر في باب رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، ومع رسول اللّٰه ﷺ مِدرى يحك به رأسه، فلما رآه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قال: (( لو أعلم أنك تنتظرني لطعنت به في عينيك )). وقال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( إنما جعل الإذن من قبل البصر )). متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦٩٠١) ومسلم (٢١٥٦). قوله: (( جحر )) أي الخرق. وقوله: (( إنما جعل الإذن )) أي أن الاستئذان مشروع مأمور به، وإنما جعل لئلا يقع البصر على الحرام، فلا يحل لأحد أن ينظر في جحر باب وغيره. وفي هذا الحديث جواز رمي عين المتطلع بشيء خفيف، فلو رماه ففقأها فلا ضمان عليه.

6899 — Sahl ibn Sa‘d reported that a man peeped through a hole in the door of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a comb-like tool with which he was scratching his head. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he said: “Had I known that you were looking at me, I would have thrust this into your eyes.”

 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٩٠٢) ومسلم (٤٤:٢١٥٨). ورواه مسلم في الآداب (٤٤:٢١٥٨) من طريق آخر بلفظ: (( من اطلع في بيت قوم بغير إذنهم، فقد حلّ لهم أن يفقؤوا عينه ))

6900 — Abu Hurairah reported that Abu al-Qasim said: “If a person were to look at you without permission and you threw a pebble at him and put out his eye, there would be no blame upon you.”
 Authentic: narrated by al-Bukhari (6902) and Muslim (44:2158). Muslim also narrated through another chain in the Book of Manners: “Whoever looks into the house of people without their permission, it becomes lawful for them to put out his eye.”

٦٩٠٢ — عن أبي ذر قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: (( من كشف ستراً فأدخل بصره في البيت قبل أن يؤذن له، فرأى عورة أهله، فقد أتى حداً لا يحل له أن يأتيه، لو أنه حين أدخل بصره استقبله رجل ففقأ عينيه ما عيّرت عليه. وإن مر الرجل على باب لا ستر له غير مغلق فنظر، فلا خطيئة عليه، إنما الخطيئة على أهل البيت)).
 حسن: رواه الترمذي (٢٧٠٧) وأحمد (٢١٣٥٩،٢١٥٧٢).
 وقوله: (( أتى حداً )). أي يستحق أن يعزر، لأنه أتى أمراً منكراً، لا يحل له أن يأتيه.
 وقوله: ما عيّرت عليه. وفي مسند أحمد: لهدرت: أي لا دية عليه.

english_source:
6902 — Abu Dharr reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever uncovers a curtain and looks into a house before being given permission, and sees the private part of its occupants, has committed a violation that is not lawful for him to commit. If a man were to confront him at that moment and put out his eyes, there would be no blame upon him. But if a man passes by a door that has no curtain and is not closed, and he looks in, then there is no sin upon him. The sin is only upon the people of the house.”
 Sound: narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2707) and Ahmad (21359, 21572).
 The phrase “has committed a violation” means that he deserves disciplinary punishment, because he has committed a forbidden and reprehensible act.
 The phrase “there would be no blame upon him” means there would be no liability or blood-money upon the one who injured him. In Musnad Ahmad the wording is: “his eye would be forfeit.”

٦٩٠٣ — عن عبد اللّٰه بن عباس قال: إن أولَ قسامة كانت في الجاهلية لفينا بني هاشم، كان رجل من بني هاشم استأجره رجل من قريش من فخذٍ أخرى، فانطلق معه في إبله، فمرَّ رجلٌ به من بني هاشم قد انقطعت عروة جوالقه فقال: أغثني بعقال أشدُّ به عروة جوالقي لا تنفر الإبل. فأعطاه عقالا، فشد به عروة جوالقه ، فلما نزلوا عقلت الإبل إلا بعيرا واحدا، فقال الذى استأجره: ما شأن هذا البعير لم يعقل من بين الإبل؟ قال: ليس له عقال. قال: فأين عقاله؟ قال: فحذفه بعصا كان فيها أجلُه، فمرَّ به رجلٌ من أهل اليمن، فقال: أتشهد الموسم؟ قال: ما أشهد، وربما شهدته. قال هل أنت مبلغ عني رسالة مرةً من الدهر قال: نعم.
 قال: فكنت إذا أنت شهدت الموسم فناد يا آل قريش، فإذا أجابوك، فناد يا آل بني هاشم. فإن أجابوك فسل عن أبي طالب، فأخبره أن فلانا قتلني فى عقال، ومات المستأجر، فلما قدم الذي استأجره أتاه أبو طالب فقال: ما فعل صاحبنا؟ قال: مرض، فأحسنتُ القيام عليه، فولِيتُ دفنه. قال: قد كان أهلَ ذاك منك. فمكث حيناً، ثم إن الرجل الذي أوصى إليه أن يُبلغ عنه وافى الموسم فقال: يا آل قريش. قالوا: هذه قريش. قال: يا آل بني هاشم. قالوا: هذه بنو هاشم. قال: أين أبو طالب؟ قالوا: هذا أبو طالب. قال: أمرني فلان أن أبلغك رسالة أن فلانا قتله في عقال. فأتاه أبو طالب فقال له: اختر منا إحدى ثلاث، إن شئت أن تؤدي مائة من الإبل، فإنك قتلت صاحبنا، وإن شئت حلف خمسون من قومك أنك لم تقتله، فإن أبيت قتلناك به، فأتى قومه، فقالوا: نحلف. فأتته امرأةٌ من بني هاشم كانت تحت رجل منهم قد ولدت له. فقالت: يا أبا طالب أُحِبُّ أن تجيز ابني هذا برجل من الخمسين ولا تُصبر يمينُه حيث تُصبر الأيمان. ففعل فأتاه رجل منهم فقال: يا أبا طالب ، أردتَ خمسين رجلا أن يحلفوا مكان مائة من الإبل ، يصيب كل رجل بعيران ، هذان بعيران فاقبلهما عني ولا تصبر يميني حيث تصبر الأيمان. فقبِلَهما، وجاء ثمانيةٌ وأربعون فحلفوا. قال ابن عباس: فوالذي نفسى بيده، ما حال الحول ومن الثمانية وأربعين عينٌ تطرِفُ.
 صحيح: رواه البخاري (٣٨٤٥)

6903 — Abdullah ibn Abbas said: The first qasamah in the pre-Islamic period among us, Banu Hashim, was that a man from Banu Hashim had been hired by a man from Quraysh, from another clan, and he went off with him among his camels. Then a man from Banu Hashim passed by him whose saddlebag strap had snapped, and he said: “Help me with a rope with which I may tie my saddlebag, so the camels do not scatter.” So he gave him a rope, and he tied his saddlebag with it. When they camped and hobbled the camels, one camel alone remained unhobbled. The man who had hired him said: “What is the matter with this camel that it alone has not been hobbled?” He replied: “It has no rope.” He said: “Where is its rope?” Then he struck him with a staff, and that was the cause of his death. A man from Yemen passed by him, and the injured man said: “Will you attend the pilgrimage season?” He said: “Usually I do not, though I may attend it.” He said: “Will you deliver a message for me at some point?” He said: “Yes.”
He said: “When you attend the pilgrimage season, call out: O Quraysh. When they answer you, call out: O Banu Hashim. When they answer you, ask for Abu Talib and tell him that so-and-so killed me over a rope.” Then the hired man died. When the man who had hired him returned, Abu Talib came to him and said: “What happened to our companion?” He said: “He became ill, so I took good care of him and handled his burial.” Abu Talib said: “You were fit to do that.” Some time passed, then the man to whom he had entrusted the message came during the pilgrimage season and called out: “O Quraysh.” They said: “This is Quraysh.” Then he called: “O Banu Hashim.” They said: “This is Banu Hashim.” He said: “Where is Abu Talib?” They said: “Here is Abu Talib.” He said: “So-and-so told me to convey a message to you: so-and-so killed me over a rope.”
Abu Talib then came to the accused and said: “Choose one of three options: either you pay one hundred camels, for you killed our companion; or fifty men from your people swear that you did not kill him; if you refuse, we will kill you in retaliation.” So he went to his people, and they said: “We will swear.” Then a woman from Banu Hashim came, married to one of those men and having borne him a child. She said: “O Abu Talib, I would like you to excuse my son from being one of the fifty and not make him swear where the oaths are sworn.” So he did. Then one of them came and said: “O Abu Talib, you wanted fifty men to swear in place of one hundred camels, which means each man’s share is two camels. Here are two camels, so accept them from me and do not make me swear where the oaths are sworn.” So he accepted them, and forty-eight men came and swore. Ibn Abbas said: By the One in whose hand is my soul, before a year had passed, not one eye among those forty-eight was still blinking.
 Authentic: narrated by al-Bukhari (3845).

6904 — A man from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, from the Ansar, reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ confirmed al-qasamah upon the way it had been in the pre-Islamic period. In another narration it adds: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ judged by it between some men of the Ansar regarding a slain man whose killing they claimed against the Jews.
 Authentic: narrated by Muslim (1670).

So Huwayyisah spoke, then Muhayyisah spoke.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said: “Either they pay blood-money for your companion, or they are notified of war.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ wrote to them about this, and they wrote back: “By Allah, we did not kill him.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Huwayyisah, Muhayyisah, and Abd al-Rahman: “Will you swear and thereby deserve the blood of your companion?” They said: “No.” He said: “Then will the Jews swear for you?” They said: “They are not Muslims.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid his blood-money from his own side. ٦٩٠٦ — عن بُشير بن يسار مولى الأنصار، عن رافع بن خديج وسهل بن أبي حثمة أنهما حدثاه: أن عبد اللّٰه بن سهل ومحيصة بن مسعود أتيا خيبر، فتفرقا في النخل، فقُتل عبد اللّٰه بن سهل. فجاء عبد الرحمن بن سهل وحويصة ومحيصة ابنا مسعود إلى النبي ﷺ، فتكلموا في أمر صاحبهم. فبدأ عبد الرحمن، وكان أصغر القوم، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( كبر الكبر )). قال يحيى: يعني ليلي الكلام الأكبر. فتكلموا في أمر صاحبهم، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( أتستحقون قتيلكم - أو قال: صاحبكم - بأيمان خمسين منكم؟ )) قالوا: يا رسول الله ﷺ، أمر لم نره. قال: (( فتبرئكم يهود بأيمان خمسين منهم؟ )) قالوا: يا رسول الله ﷺ، قوم كفار. فوداه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ من قبله. قال سهل: فأدركت ناقة من تلك الإبل فدخلت مربداً فركضتني برجلها.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٤٢، ٦١٤٣)، ومسلم (١٦٦٩/٢). واللفظ للبخاري.

6906 — Bushayr ibn Yasar, the freedman of the Ansar, reported from Rafi ibn Khadij and Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah that Abdullah ibn Sahl and Muhayyisah ibn Masud came to Khaybar and then separated among the palm groves. Abdullah ibn Sahl was killed. Then Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahl, Huwayyisah, and Muhayyisah, the sons of Masud, came to the Prophet ﷺ and spoke regarding their companion. Abd al-Rahman began speaking, and he was the youngest of the group, so the Prophet ﷺ said: “Let the elder speak, let the elder speak.” Yahya said: This means the oldest should be the one to speak first.
Then they spoke regarding their companion, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Will you establish your claim to your slain man,” or he said, “your companion,” “by fifty oaths from among you?” They said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is something we did not witness.” He said: “Then the Jews will clear themselves by fifty oaths from among them.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they are disbelieving people.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid the blood-money himself.
 Sahl said: One she-camel from those camels caught up with me, entered an enclosure, and kicked me with its leg.
 Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (6142, 6143) and Muslim (2:1669). This wording is from al-Bukhari.

٦٩٠٦ — عن بُشير بن يسار مولى الأنصار، عن رافع بن خديج وسهل بن أبي حثمة أنهما حدثاه: أن عبد اللّٰه بن سهل ومحيصة بن مسعود أتيا خيبر، فتفرقا في النخل، فقُتل عبد اللّٰه بن سهل. فجاء عبد الرحمن بن سهل وحويصة ومحيصة ابنا مسعود إلى النبي ﷺ، فتكلموا في أمر صاحبهم. فبدأ عبد الرحمن، وكان أصغر القوم، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( كبر الكبر )). قال يحيى: يعني ليلي الكلام الأكبر. فتكلموا في أمر صاحبهم، فقال النبي ﷺ: (( أتستحقون قتيلكم - أو قال: صاحبكم - بأيمان خمسين منكم؟ )) قالوا: يا رسول الله ﷺ، أمر لم نره. قال: (( فتبرئكم يهود بأيمان خمسين منهم؟ )) قالوا: يا رسول الله ﷺ، قوم كفار. فوداه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ من قبله. قال سهل: فأدركت ناقة من تلك الإبل فدخلت مربداً فركضتني برجلها.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٦١٤٢، ٦١٤٣)، ومسلم (١٦٦٩/٢). واللفظ للبخاري.
6906 — Bushayr ibn Yasar, the freedman of the Ansar, reported from Rafi ibn Khadij and Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah that Abdullah ibn Sahl and Muhayyisah ibn Masud came to Khaybar and then separated among the palm groves. Abdullah ibn Sahl was killed. Then Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahl, Huwayyisah, and Muhayyisah, the sons of Masud, came to the Prophet ﷺ and spoke regarding their companion. Abd al-Rahman began speaking, and he was the youngest of the group, so the Prophet ﷺ said: “Let the elder speak, let the elder speak.” Yahya said: This means the oldest should be the one to speak first.
Then they spoke regarding their companion, and the Prophet ﷺ said: “Will you establish your claim to your slain man,” or he said, “your companion,” “by fifty oaths from among you?” They said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is something we did not witness.” He said: “Then the Jews will clear themselves by fifty oaths from among them.” They said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they are disbelieving people.” So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid the blood-money himself.
 Sahl said: One she-camel from those camels caught up with me, entered an enclosure, and kicked me with its leg.
 Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (6142, 6143) and Muslim (2:1669). This wording is from al-Bukhari.

6907 — Bushayr ibn Yasar claimed that a man from the Ansar called Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah informed him that some men from his people went to Khaybar and separated there. They found one of them murdered, and they said to those among whom he was found: “You killed our companion.” They said: “We did not kill him, nor do we know any killer.” So they went to the Prophet ﷺ and said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we went to Khaybar and found one of us murdered.” He said: “Let the elders speak, let the elders speak.” Then he said to them: “Will you bring proof against the one who killed him?” They said: “We have no proof.” He said: “Then they will swear.” They said: “We do not accept the oaths of the Jews.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked allowing his blood to go to waste, so he paid his blood-money with one hundred camels from the alms camels.
 Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (6898) and Muslim (5:1669).
 This report is abbreviated by some narrators. Its fuller meaning is that the Prophet ﷺ first asked the Ansar for evidence. When they said they had none, he then said: “Then you may swear and deserve the blood of your companion.” They said: “How can we swear?” So he said: “Then they will swear.” In this way, the meaning is complete and the reports do not contradict one another.

arabic_source:
٦٩٠٨ — عن أبي قلابة:
أن عمر بن عبد العزيز أبرز سريره يومًا للناس، ثم أذن لهم فدخلوا، فقال:
ما تقولون في القسامة؟
قالوا:
نقول: القسامة القود بها حق، وقد أقادت بها الخلفاء.
قال لي:
ما تقول يا أبا قلابة؟
ونصبني للناس.
فقلت:
يا أمير المؤمنين، عندك رؤوس الأجناد وأشراف العرب، أرأيت لو أن خمسين منهم شهدوا على رجل محصن بدمشق أنه قد زنى، لم يروه، أكنت ترجمه؟
قال:
لا.
قلت:
أرأيت لو أن خمسين منهم شهدوا على رجل بحمص أنه سرق، أكنت تقطعه ولم يروه؟
قال:
لا.
قلت:
فوالله ما قتل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قط إلا في إحدى ثلاث خصال: رجل قتل بجريرة نفسه فقتل، أو رجل زنى بعد إحصان، أو رجل حارب الله ورسوله وارتد عن الإسلام.
فقال القوم:
أوليس قد حدث أنس بن مالك أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قطع في السرق، وسمر الأعين، ثم نبذهم في الشمس؟
فقلت:
أنا أحدثكم حديث أنس.
حدثني أنس أن نفرًا من عكل، ثمانية، قدموا على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فبايعوه على الإسلام، فاستوخموا الأرض فسقمت أجسامهم، فشكوا ذلك إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
قال:
«أَفَلَا تَخْرُجُونَ مَعَ رَاعِينَا فِي إِبِلِهِ، فَتُصِيبُونَ مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا؟»
قالوا:
بلى.
فخرجوا، فشربوا من ألبانها وأبوالها فصحوا، فقتلوا راعي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وأطردوا النعم.
فبلغ ذلك رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأرسل في آثارهم، فأدركوا فجيء بهم، فأمر بهم، فقطعت أيديهم وأرجلهم، وسمرت أعينهم، ثم نبذوا في الشمس حتى ماتوا.
قلت:
وأي شيء أشد مما صنع هؤلاء؟ ارتدوا عن الإسلام، وقتلوا، وسرقوا.
فقال عنبسة بن سعيد:
والله إن سمعت كاليوم قط.
فقلت:
أترد علي حديثي يا عنبسة؟
قال:
لا، ولكن جئت بالحديث على وجهه. والله لا يزال هذا الجند بخير ما عاش هذا الشيخ بين أظهرهم.
قلت:
وقد كان في هذا سنة من رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: دخل عليه نفر من الأنصار فتحدثوا عنده، فخرج رجل منهم بين أيديهم فقتل، فخرجوا بعده، فإذا هم بصاحبهم يتشحط في الدم.
فرجعوا إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقالوا:
يا رسول الله ﷺ، صاحبنا كان يتحدث معنا، فخرج بين أيدينا، فإذا نحن به يتشحط في الدم.
فخرج رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال:
«بِمَنْ تَظُنُّونَ، أَوْ تَرَوْنَ، قَتَلَهُ؟»
قالوا:
نرى أن اليهود قتلته.
فأرسل إلى اليهود فدعاهم، فقال:
«أَنْتُمْ قَتَلْتُمْ هَذَا؟»
قالوا:
لا.
قال:
«أَتَرْضَوْنَ نَفْلَ خَمْسِينَ مِنَ الْيَهُودِ مَا قَتَلُوهُ؟»
فقالوا:
ما يبالون أن يقتلونا أجمعين ثم ينتفلون.
قال:
«أَفَتَسْتَحِقُّونَ الدِّيَةَ بِأَيْمَانِ خَمْسِينَ مِنْكُمْ؟»
قالوا:
ما كنا لنحلف.
فوداه من عنده.
قلت:
وقد كانت هذيل خلعوا خليعًا لهم في الجاهلية، فطرق أهل بيت من اليمن بالبطحاء، فانتبه له رجل منهم فحذفه بالسيف فقتله.
فجاءت هذيل فأخذوا اليماني، فرفعوه إلى عمر بالموسم، وقالوا:
قتل صاحبنا.
فقال:
إنهم قد خلعوه.
فقال:
يقسم خمسون من هذيل ما خلعوه.
فأقسم منهم تسعة وأربعون رجلًا، وقدم رجل منهم من الشام، فسألوه أن يقسم، فافتدى يمينه منهم بألف درهم، فأدخلوا مكانه رجلًا آخر.
فدفعه إلى أخي المقتول، فقرنت يده بيده.
قالوا:
فانطلقا والخمسون الذين أقسموا، حتى إذا كانوا بنخلة أخذتهم السماء، فدخلوا في غار في الجبل، فانهجم الغار على الخمسين الذين أقسموا فماتوا جميعًا.
وأفلت القرينان، واتبعهما حجر فكسر رجل أخي المقتول، فعاش حولًا ثم مات.
قلت:
وقد كان عبد الملك بن مروان أقاد رجلًا بالقسامة، ثم ندم بعد ما صنع، فأمر بالخمسين الذين أقسموا فمحوا من الديوان، وسيرهم إلى الشام.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٨٩٩)، ومسلم (١٦٧١/١٠)، والسياق للبخاري.
وطريق الجمع بين هذا الحديث والأحاديث التي قبله أن يقال: حفظ بعضهم ما لم يحفظ الآخر. وتفصيله أن النبي ﷺ طلب البينة أولًا من المدعين وهم الأنصار، فلما لم تكن عندهم البينة عرض عليهم الأيمان فامتنعوا، ثم عرض عليهم تحليف اليهود فأبوا، فوداه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ من عنده من بيت المال، حتى لا يتعارض بعض الحديث مع بعض، والقصة واحدة.

6908 — Abū Qilābah reported:
One day ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz brought out his couch for the people and then permitted them to enter. He asked:
“What do you say concerning al-qasāmah?”
They replied:
“We hold that retaliation may validly be established through al-qasāmah, and the caliphs have carried out retaliation by means of it.”
He asked me:
“What do you say, O Abū Qilābah?”
And he brought me forward before the people.
I said:
“O Commander of the Believers, you have with you the commanders of the armies and the nobles of the Arabs. Suppose fifty of them testified against a previously married man in Damascus that he had committed adultery, although they had not actually seen it. Would you stone him?”
He replied:
“No.”
I said:
“Suppose fifty of them testified against a man in Ḥimṣ that he had stolen, although they had not seen him do it. Would you cut off his hand?”
He replied:
“No.”
I said:
“By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never put anyone to death except for one of three matters: a man who killed and was killed for his own crime; a man who committed adultery after having been married; or a man who fought Allah and His Messenger and apostatized from Islam.”
The people said:
“Did Anas ibn Mālik not report that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cut off hands and branded eyes, then left those people in the sun?”
I said:
“I will relate to you the hadith of Anas.”
Anas told me that eight men from ʿUkl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and pledged allegiance to Islam. They found the climate unhealthy, and their bodies became ill, so they complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He said:
“Why do you not go out with our shepherd among his camels and drink some of their milk and urine?”
They replied:
“Yes.”
They went out, drank their milk and urine, and recovered. Then they killed the shepherd of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and drove away the camels.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ learned of this, he sent men after them. They were caught and brought back. He ordered that their hands and feet be cut off and their eyes branded, and then they were left in the sun until they died.
I said:
“What could be more serious than what these people did? They apostatized from Islam, killed, and stole.”
ʿAnbasah ibn Saʿīd said:
“By Allah, I have never heard anything like what I heard today.”
I asked:
“Are you rejecting my hadith, O ʿAnbasah?”
He replied:
“No. Rather, you have presented the hadith in its complete form. By Allah, this army will remain upon good so long as this old man remains among them.”
I said:
“There was also a precedent from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning this matter. A group of the Anṣār entered upon him and spoke with him. One of them left ahead of the others and was killed. When the others went out, they found their companion writhing in his blood.
They returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:
‘O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, our companion was speaking with us, then he went out ahead of us, and we found him writhing in his blood.’
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out and asked:
‘Whom do you suspect—or whom do you think—killed him?’
They replied:
‘We think the Jews killed him.’
He sent for the Jews and summoned them, then asked:
‘Did you kill this man?’
They replied:
‘No.’
He asked the Anṣār:
‘Would you accept fifty Jews swearing that they did not kill him?’
They replied:
‘They would not care if they killed all of us and then swore falsely.’
He said:
‘Then will you become entitled to the blood-money by fifty oaths from among yourselves?’
They replied:
‘We would not swear.’
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paid his blood-money himself.
I also said:
“In the pre-Islamic period, Hudhayl had formally disowned one of their men. He came by night to a household from Yemen at al-Baṭḥāʾ. A man among them awoke and struck him with a sword, killing him.
Hudhayl seized the Yemeni and brought him before ʿUmar during the pilgrimage season, saying:
‘He killed our companion.’
ʿUmar said:
‘They had disowned him.’
He then ordered:
‘Let fifty men from Hudhayl swear that they had not disowned him.’
Forty-nine men swore. Then a man among them arrived from Syria, and they asked him to swear. He bought himself out of taking the oath by giving them one thousand dirhams, so they substituted another man in his place.
That man was handed over to the murdered man’s brother, and their hands were tied together.
They set out together with the fifty men who had sworn. When they reached Nakhlah, a storm overtook them, so they entered a cave in the mountain. The cave collapsed upon the fifty men who had sworn, and all of them died.
The two men tied together escaped, but a rock followed them and broke the leg of the murdered man’s brother. He lived for one year and then died.”
I also said:
“ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān once executed a man on the basis of al-qasāmah, but afterward regretted what he had done. He ordered that the fifty men who had sworn be removed from the official register and sent away to Syria.”
Authentic: Narrated by al-Bukhārī (6899) and Muslim (1671/10). This is the wording of al-Bukhārī.
The way to reconcile this hadith with the preceding reports is that some narrators preserved details that others did not. The complete sequence is that the Prophet ﷺ first asked the claimants—the Anṣār—for evidence. When they had no evidence, he offered them the option of taking the oaths, but they refused. He then offered to have the Jews swear, but they refused to accept their oaths. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ therefore paid the blood-money himself from the public treasury. In this way the narrations do not contradict one another; they concern the same incident.

٦٩٠٨ — عن أبي قلابة:
أن عمر بن عبد العزيز أبرز سريره يومًا للناس، ثم أذن لهم فدخلوا، فقال:
ما تقولون في القسامة؟

لا.

٦٩٠٨ — عن أبي قلابة:
أن عمر بن عبد العزيز أبرز سريره يومًا للناس، ثم أذن لهم فدخلوا، فقال:
ما تقولون في القسامة؟
قالوا:
نقول: القسامة القود بها حق، وقد أقادت بها الخلفاء.
قال لي:
ما تقول يا أبا قلابة؟
ونصبني للناس.
فقلت:
يا أمير المؤمنين، عندك رؤوس الأجناد وأشراف العرب، أرأيت لو أن خمسين منهم شهدوا على رجل محصن بدمشق أنه قد زنى، لم يروه، أكنت ترجمه؟
قال:
لا.
قلت:
أرأيت لو أن خمسين منهم شهدوا على رجل بحمص أنه سرق، أكنت تقطعه ولم يروه؟
قال:
لا.
قلت:
فوالله ما قتل رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قط إلا في إحدى ثلاث خصال: رجل قتل بجريرة نفسه فقتل، أو رجل زنى بعد إحصان، أو رجل حارب الله ورسوله وارتد عن الإسلام.
فقال القوم:
أوليس قد حدث أنس بن مالك أن رسول اللّٰه ﷺ قطع في السرق، وسمر الأعين، ثم نبذهم في الشمس؟
فقلت:
أنا أحدثكم حديث أنس.
حدثني أنس أن نفرًا من عكل، ثمانية، قدموا على رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فبايعوه على الإسلام، فاستوخموا الأرض فسقمت أجسامهم، فشكوا ذلك إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ.
قال:
«أَفَلَا تَخْرُجُونَ مَعَ رَاعِينَا فِي إِبِلِهِ، فَتُصِيبُونَ مِنْ أَلْبَانِهَا وَأَبْوَالِهَا؟»
قالوا:
بلى.
فخرجوا، فشربوا من ألبانها وأبوالها فصحوا، فقتلوا راعي رسول اللّٰه ﷺ وأطردوا النعم.
فبلغ ذلك رسول اللّٰه ﷺ، فأرسل في آثارهم، فأدركوا فجيء بهم، فأمر بهم، فقطعت أيديهم وأرجلهم، وسمرت أعينهم، ثم نبذوا في الشمس حتى ماتوا.
قلت:
وأي شيء أشد مما صنع هؤلاء؟ ارتدوا عن الإسلام، وقتلوا، وسرقوا.
فقال عنبسة بن سعيد:
والله إن سمعت كاليوم قط.
فقلت:
أترد علي حديثي يا عنبسة؟
قال:
لا، ولكن جئت بالحديث على وجهه. والله لا يزال هذا الجند بخير ما عاش هذا الشيخ بين أظهرهم.
قلت:
وقد كان في هذا سنة من رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: دخل عليه نفر من الأنصار فتحدثوا عنده، فخرج رجل منهم بين أيديهم فقتل، فخرجوا بعده، فإذا هم بصاحبهم يتشحط في الدم.
فرجعوا إلى رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقالوا:
يا رسول الله ﷺ، صاحبنا كان يتحدث معنا، فخرج بين أيدينا، فإذا نحن به يتشحط في الدم.
فخرج رسول اللّٰه ﷺ فقال:
«بِمَنْ تَظُنُّونَ، أَوْ تَرَوْنَ، قَتَلَهُ؟»
قالوا:
نرى أن اليهود قتلته.
فأرسل إلى اليهود فدعاهم، فقال:
«أَنْتُمْ قَتَلْتُمْ هَذَا؟»
قالوا:
لا.
قال:
«أَتَرْضَوْنَ نَفْلَ خَمْسِينَ مِنَ الْيَهُودِ مَا قَتَلُوهُ؟»
فقالوا:
ما يبالون أن يقتلونا أجمعين ثم ينتفلون.
قال:
«أَفَتَسْتَحِقُّونَ الدِّيَةَ بِأَيْمَانِ خَمْسِينَ مِنْكُمْ؟»
قالوا:
ما كنا لنحلف.
فوداه من عنده.
قلت:
وقد كانت هذيل خلعوا خليعًا لهم في الجاهلية، فطرق أهل بيت من اليمن بالبطحاء، فانتبه له رجل منهم فحذفه بالسيف فقتله.
فجاءت هذيل فأخذوا اليماني، فرفعوه إلى عمر بالموسم، وقالوا:
قتل صاحبنا.
فقال:
إنهم قد خلعوه.
فقال:
يقسم خمسون من هذيل ما خلعوه.
فأقسم منهم تسعة وأربعون رجلًا، وقدم رجل منهم من الشام، فسألوه أن يقسم، فافتدى يمينه منهم بألف درهم، فأدخلوا مكانه رجلًا آخر.
فدفعه إلى أخي المقتول، فقرنت يده بيده.
قالوا:
فانطلقا والخمسون الذين أقسموا، حتى إذا كانوا بنخلة أخذتهم السماء، فدخلوا في غار في الجبل، فانهجم الغار على الخمسين الذين أقسموا فماتوا جميعًا.
وأفلت القرينان، واتبعهما حجر فكسر رجل أخي المقتول، فعاش حولًا ثم مات.
قلت:
وقد كان عبد الملك بن مروان أقاد رجلًا بالقسامة، ثم ندم بعد ما صنع، فأمر بالخمسين الذين أقسموا فمحوا من الديوان، وسيرهم إلى الشام.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٦٨٩٩)، ومسلم (١٦٧١/١٠)، والسياق للبخاري.
وطريق الجمع بين هذا الحديث والأحاديث التي قبله أن يقال: حفظ بعضهم ما لم يحفظ الآخر. وتفصيله أن النبي ﷺ طلب البينة أولًا من المدعين وهم الأنصار، فلما لم تكن عندهم البينة عرض عليهم الأيمان فامتنعوا، ثم عرض عليهم تحليف اليهود فأبوا، فوداه رسول اللّٰه ﷺ من عنده من بيت المال، حتى لا يتعارض بعض الحديث مع بعض، والقصة واحدة.

“What do you say concerning al-qasāmah?”
They replied:
“We hold that retaliation may validly be established through al-qasāmah, and the caliphs have carried out retaliation by means of it.”
He asked me:
“What do you say, O Abū Qilābah?”
And he brought me forward before the people.
I said:
“O Commander of the Believers, you have with you the commanders of the armies and the nobles of the Arabs. Suppose fifty of them testified against a previously married man in Damascus that he had committed adultery, although they had not actually seen it. Would you stone him?”
He replied:
“No.”
I said:
“Suppose fifty of them testified against a man in Ḥimṣ that he had stolen, although they had not seen him do it. Would you cut off his hand?”
He replied:
“No.”

“By Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ never put anyone to death except for one of three matters: a man who killed and was killed for his own crime; a man who committed adultery after having been married; or a man who fought Allah and His Messenger and apostatized from Islam.”

“I will relate to you the hadith of Anas.”

ʿUmar said:

They told him that al-qasamah was applied among them, in Banu Harithah ibn al-Harith, regarding a man from the Ansar called Abdullah ibn Sahl who was killed at Khaybar. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: “Will fifty of you swear so that you may deserve your slain man,” or he said, “your companion?” They said: “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we neither witnessed nor were present.” Bushayr claimed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said to them: “Then the Jews will clear themselves by fifty oaths,” and then he mentioned the rest of the story.
 Sound: narrated by al-Bayhaqi (8/119).
